content: The PanoRef coverage optimizer implementation was reviewed and found to correctly implement the designed algorithm architecture (deterministic area-proportional sampling, joint-pair evaluation, shared coarse-to-fine engine) for normal graybox sets, but with significant blockers for complex imported sets. Key issues identified: (1) imported sets can produce zero legal candidates because the entire object AABB is used for clearance rather than actual geometry; (2) geometry representation won't scale to heavy imports due to JavaScript object overhead and GC pressure from triangle expansion; (3) geometry extraction still blocks the main thread before worker transfer; (4) the UI incorrectly allows rewriting origins of existing panoramas, which ruins alignment; (5) reachableCoverage and combinedCoverage use incompatible sample banks (coarse vs fine with different seeds); (6) fixed-first mode doesn't enforce minimum origin separation; (7) the 'four-level refinement' is not truly iterative—it samples around the original seed rather than updating the center after each level; (8) local candidates can float between floors on sloped/multilevel terrain; (9) the optimizer and runtime renderer use different quality rules (angle/texel vs distance-only blending). A patch was applied to align the shader with the optimizer's quality function (projectedQualityAt, winner-takes-most weighting with dominance modes), removing the stale PROJECTED_FALLOFF constant and projectedConfidence. Tests were updated accordingly and passed (36 tests in multiOriginInteraction.test.ts). Full test suite ran: 371 tests passed across 42 test files, lint passed (tsc --noEmit), build succeeded (1777 modules transformed). The reviewer concluded the implementation is promising but not production-ready for complex imported sets, recommending: replace AABB clearance with geometry clearance, use typed arrays/transferable buffers, move extraction into worker, remove ability to relocate existing panorama references, recalculate metrics on one common sample bank, enforce separation in fixed-first mode, and reproject local refinement candidates onto their floor. A follow-up instruction was given to rebase onto main, add allowed-floor-region mechanism, run a real complex imported-set benchmark with 100K+ optimizer integration test, and use a subagent to disprove completeness iteratively.

The PanoRef coverage optimizer patch adds an explicit allowed-floor-region mechanism to handle geometrically ambiguous large horizontal surfaces (roofs, platforms, prop tops) in complex imported sets. The implementation adds an optional `allowedFloorRegions` field to `CoverageSceneData`, normalizes and validates user-supplied world-space bounds, filters floor triangles by AABB intersection with those regions, and constrains candidate generation to points inside the allowed regions. The UI exposes a toggle and editable X/Y/Z min/max inputs, defaulting to a region around the capture origin. A new test verifies that a 6×6 floor plus a disconnected 3×3 tabletop at y=0.8–1.5 is filtered to only the floor triangles when an allowed region of ±3.1 in X/Z and ±0.1 in Y is supplied, and that generated candidates all sit at the expected camera height. Documentation and regression-audit notes were updated to describe the new capability. An earlier patch attempt failed because the README line it targeted had already been modified; the successful patch applied the core engine/UI/test changes without that README edit. The broader context remains that the implementation is promising but not yet production-ready for complex imported sets, with the allowed-floor-region mechanism being one of several recommended fixes still in progress alongside rebasing, publishing, and adversarial auditing.

After fixing TypeScript errors in `surfaceSampler.ts` (Vec3 casting) and `CoverageOptimizerPanel.tsx` (removing invalid `key` props on Field elements and restructuring the axis map), tests (87 tests across projectionCoverage, multiOriginInteraction, uiFidelity), lint, and build all passed, and an E2E test for the coverage optimizer was added to verify the floor region toggle, invalid bound detection, and that props/rooftops do not become candidate platforms. The broader context remains that the implementation is promising but not yet production-ready for complex imported sets, with the allowed-floor-region mechanism being one of several recommended fixes still in progress alongside rebasing, publishing, and adversarial auditing.

Round three adversarial audit of commit 4153429 identified two stale-state holes: editing bounds after a completed run leaves the old result and origin-apply actions visible even when origins fall outside the newly displayed region, and changing the primary panorama does not refresh the untouched default region or invalidate a fixed-first result, leaving the region centered on the previous panorama. The in-flight locking fix itself works. A follow-up patch centralizes result invalidation for every optimizer input and synchronizes only untouched default bounds to the active capture origin while preserving user-authored bounds. The patch adds a defaultFloorRegion helper, a floorRegionTouchedRef, a captureInputKey derived from primaryPano id/origin/size/cameraHeight, a previousCaptureInputKeyRef, and an invalidateAnalysis function; it wires a useEffect to invalidate and, when the user has not touched the floor region, reset the default floor region on capture-origin/size/height changes, and routes mode, restrictFloorRegion, and floor min/max changes through invalidateAnalysis while marking floorRegionTouchedRef on manual edits. An E2E step was added to fill the X minimum to -4 and assert zero results and zero apply-capture buttons. Lint, the projectionCoverage/multiOriginInteraction/uiFidelity test suites, and the build were run after the patch; their outcomes are still pending at snapshot time. PR #23 (head 4153429) is MERGEABLE with mergeStateStatus UNSTABLE.
